scenarioResults.note: REFERENCE: genuinely cold Chrome relaunch with every emulator route aborted renders all 3 protected rows fromCache:true in 26ms; anonymous auth uid restored offline from IndexedDB. Caveat observed: if the persistence lease is still held by a dying predecessor, the SDK silently falls back to an EMPTY memory cache (0 rows, fromCache:true, no error surface) — forceOwnership:true required for restart-shaped lifecycles

REFERENCE: freshness honesty is one boolean (snapshot.metadata.fromCache) surfaced per snapshot — rendered offline as fromCache:true, settling to false on reconnect. No per-query retention fact, no refusal contract: protected rows ARE cold-retained for whoever holds the device profile; rules are not re-evaluated for cached reads offline

REFERENCE: offline create+update render immediately beside the 3 cached rows (4 rows, pending=true, 68ms), survive a full browser restart while still offline (first post-restart snapshot: 4 rows fromCache with the queued write still pending, 24ms), and the second client proves no remote commit pre-reconnect (sees exactly 3 rows). The queue itself is opaque: no enumerable outbox, no per-intent identity/sequence surface — hasPendingWrites booleans only

REFERENCE: offline-vs-online same-field conflict settles deterministically in server-apply order — the reconnecting client's queued update lands after the online edit and wins the field; both clients converge to the identical final value. Blind last-write-wins: no revision check, no conflict surfaced to either client

REFERENCE: reconnect renders cache-first (25ms, 4 rows pending) then flushes and settles (hasPendingWrites false, fromCache false) by 75ms; exactly one document for the queued create (deterministic doc id via setDoc — dedupe is the author's job, not a settlement ledger); second client converges live. Settlement evidence is thin: write promises resolve, but there is no receipt/changed-count/version envelope to assert against

differentiators.observation: REFERENCE BAR (what good looks like on the floor): cached rows AND durable queued writes render together after an offline restart — the exact combination Snapback's LLP 0090 D3 rule forecloses today (0137-a1-f6). Firebase pays for it with blind overlays (no derived-plan proof) and silent LWW conflicts.
differentiators.mustNotRegress: Not a Snapback surface — reference observation for the D3 design decision.

differentiators.observation: REFERENCE CONTRAST (where the Snapback arm is already stronger): Firebase's floor has no honesty contract beyond one fromCache boolean — no retention facts, no refusal codes, protected rows cold-retained without lease custody, silent empty-cache fallback when the persistence lease is contended, no outbox inspection, no settlement envelopes. Snapback's refuse-with-clarity handles, coded refusals, enumerable outbox, and receipted settlement are ahead of this reference on every evidence axis.
differentiators.mustNotRegress: Snapback's retention/settlement honesty surfaces (0137 A1 arm differentiators) while closing the D3/render gap.
